description: A single measured value about a Participant: a lab result, vital sign, anthropometric, physiologic or imaging measurement. One source row can produce several MeasurementObservations. Required slots: associated_participant and observation_type; every other slot is optional. Fill exactly one value_* slot.

The lower limit of the REFERENCE (normal) range for this result, as supplied by the laboratory or the reference equation. It is NOT a limit of detection. A Quantity in the same unit as value_quantity; leave empty when the source gives no reference range. A result below the assay's detection limit goes in value_quantity with Quantity.operator LESS_THAN and the detection limit as the number. BDC-HM has no limit-of-detection slot; if one is needed, raise it with HM.
Example source variable description: Lower limit of normal FEV1 (mL), LFEV1 [Pulmonary Function Test. PULP and PULB (pre and post bronchodilator). Visit 5]

description: The upper limit of the REFERENCE (normal) range for this result, as supplied by the laboratory or the reference equation. It is NOT an upper limit of detection or of the measurable range. A Quantity in the same unit as value_quantity; leave empty when the source gives no reference range. A result above the measurable range goes in value_quantity with Quantity.operator GREATER_THAN.

Required. The code for what was measured. It must be a permissible value of MeasurementObservationTypeEnum on BDC-HM main: a closed list of CURIEs from OBA, OMOP (LOINC, SNOMED), CMO, EFO, NCIT and similar. Any other code fails validation. Take the code from the Variables file, using the most specific code the source variable supports. If the right code is not yet in the enum, do not use it: confirm it in its source ontology, open a BDC-HM issue to add it, and hold the mapping until it is merged.

This slot will be an identifier to a File, QuestionnaireResponse, or Assay. Use this to link a measurement observation to an entity that generated it. For example, a CESD score should have a link to the QuestionnaireResponse from which it is derived.

Where on the body the measurement was taken, when that matters to the value and is not already part of observation_type: the arm used for blood pressure, the ankle artery for ankle-brachial index, the carotid segment for intima-media thickness. The value is a BodySite object, not a bare code: BodySite.site holds an Uberon CURIE (required) and BodySite.qualifier holds laterality or another refinement, such as right. Free text such as 'Right arm' is not valid. Not used for blood or urine assays: the specimen is part of observation_type.
The object that fills body_site. It holds site (required) and qualifier (optional).

Required. An Uberon CURIE for the anatomical site; it must be a subclass of UBERON:0001062 anatomical entity (AnatomicSiteEnum). Codes checked in OLS4: UBERON:0001460 arm; UBERON:0004454 tarsal region (synonym: ankle); UBERON:0001398 brachial artery; UBERON:0001538 posterior tibial artery; UBERON:0001539 dorsalis pedis artery; UBERON:0010197 trunk of common carotid artery; UBERON:0037468 waist; UBERON:0001464 hip; UBERON:0000916 abdomen.

Optional; may hold several values. Free text that refines site: laterality (right, left), upper or lower, or containment. Blood pressure taken in the right arm = site UBERON:0001460 with qualifier right.

Use this slot to specify what position the Participant was in when the measurement was taken in those instances where those are relevant. Examples include blood pressure and height. Body position does not matter for measurements resulting from blood or urine assays, for example.
The patient is in a sitting position during the measurement or observation
The patient is in a standing position during the measurement or observation
Example source variable description: First standing systolic blood pressure [Ankle Brachial BP (Blood Pressure - ultrasound work station). Visit 3]

description: The patient is lying on their back during the measurement or observation
The patient is lying on their stomach during the measurement or observation
Use this slot to specify the occupation of the person who collected the measurement. This is often specified for blood pressure measurements.
A medical doctor (MD) or doctor of osteopathic medicine (DO)
A registered nurse (RN), licensed practical nurse (LPN), or other nursing professional
A healthcare worker trained to perform specific technical tasks
Any other type of healthcare professional involved in performing an activity

Use when the value summarizes several readings instead of being a single reading. An average of repeated blood pressure readings is AVERAGE; a spirometry 'best' or 'highest acceptable' effort is MAXIMUM; the first or last reading of a series is FIRST_MEASUREMENT or LAST_MEASUREMENT. Leave empty for a single reading. One value only. Do not write 'average' or 'best' into method_type instead.
An average or mean of measurements taken across a time period
Example source variable description: Average of 2nd and 3rd systolic bp measures|[Computed net average of second and third blood pressure measurement]. 2nd and 3rd systolic. Q21 [Siting Blood Pressure. SBPA. Visit 1]

description: The minimum value among measurements taken across a time period. Sometimes a measurement will be listed as best or worst. Whether or not this translates to a minimum or maximum depends on the measurements and what it means for disease state or organ function.

The maximum value among measurements taken across a time period. Sometimes a measurement will be listed as best or worst. Whether or not this translates to a minimum or maximum depends on the measurements and what it means for disease state or organ function.
Example source variable description: Forced Expiratory Volume at 1 second (FEV1) - Highest value among acceptable maneuvers

description: The sum of measurements taken across a time period
The first measurement taken in a series of measurements across a time period.
Example source variable description: First standing systolic blood pressure [Ankle Brachial BP (Blood Pressure - ultrasound work station). Visit 3]

description: The last measurement taken in a series of measurements across a time period.

Optional; may hold several values. Must be values of InstrumentEnum: BioAssay Ontology (BAO) subclasses of BAO:0003118 instrument. These are laboratory instruments such as plate readers, mass spectrometers, PCR systems, flow cytometers and HPLC systems (BAO:0002733 HPLC System). Clinical devices (sphygmomanometer, oscillometric monitor, spirometer, ECG, CT or MRI scanner, echocardiography machine) are not in this enum: leave instrument empty and name the device type in method_type. Fill only when the source names the instrument. A needed clinical-device value is a BDC-HM gap; raise an issue.
Use this slot to link a MeasurementObservation to a specific visit or exam.
Required. Use this slot to link a MeasurementObservation to a specific Participant

Use this slot to specify the age of the Participant at the time of the MeasurementObservation. This will often be the same as the age at visit, but not always. An example, is when a Participant gives a weight at a specific, previous age. BDC-HM stores this as an integer number of DAYS. A source age in years is multiplied by 365 (the production convention) and rounded to a whole number; a source age already in days is used as is.

Use this slot to specify the method used to make the observation. Examples include anthropometry, ultrasound, CBC, and calculation. Free text. Use it for the technique that tells otherwise comparable values apart: the assay type (for example immunoturbidimetric, enzymatic, high-sensitivity immunoassay); the blood pressure device type (random-zero sphygmomanometer, standard sphygmomanometer, automated oscillometric device); the imaging or echocardiography method (for example M-mode, 2D biplane Simpson, cardiac CT); for spirometry predicted and percent-predicted values, the reference equation (for example Hankinson NHANES III, GLI-2012); and for a calculated value, the formula or equation (for example Friedewald for LDL, CKD-EPI 2009 or 2021 for eGFR). Do not use method_type for anything that has its own slot: fasting and bronchodilator status go in context, averages and best efforts in qualifier, posture in body_position, site in body_site.
Example source variable description: Glucose Method|DLco % predicted GLI|V1 Calibrated Serum Creatinine mg/dL

description: Use this slot to specify the Organization that performed the measurement. This will often be a clinic or an analytical lab.

Use this slot to contain the value of the MeasurementObservation if that value is a String. Last resort: only for a result that is text and cannot be written as a number (value_quantity) or a permissible enum value (value_enum). A result such as '<0.15' is not a string: write it as value_quantity with operator LESS_THAN. Fill exactly one value_* slot per MeasurementObservation.
Use this slot to contain the value of the MeasurementObservation if that value is a Boolean. Only when a true/false finding is itself the measurement.

Use this slot to contain the value of the MeasurementObservation if that value is an Integer or Decimal. It is a Quantity object: the number in value_decimal or value_integer, plus the unit (the concept's target unit). This is the slot for almost every MeasurementObservation concept.

Use this slot when the value is one of the coded values BDC-HM enumerates in BaseObservationValueEnum: smoking status (SmokingStatusObservationTypeEnum), educational attainment (EducationalAttainmentObservationTypeEnum) and occupation (OccupationTypeEnum). Among the MeasurementObservation concepts only Cigarette smoking status fits. Write the BDC-HM permissible-value NAME (for example CURRENT_SMOKER, UNKNOWN), not its OMOP meaning code. Exception: OccupationTypeEnum value names are themselves CURIEs (for example OMOP:36311194), so for occupation the name as HM defines it is the CURIE. Production cig_smok writes the OMOP meaning code (for example OMOP:45883537) instead of the name; that is a known production departure pending Anne's decision (see questions). Any other coded result has no valid value here; that is a BDC-HM gap, so raise an issue rather than writing free text.
The participant currently smokes cigarettes (BDC-HM meaning OMOP:40766945)
The participant smoked cigarettes in the past but does not now (BDC-HM meaning OMOP:45883458)
The participant has never smoked cigarettes (BDC-HM meaning OMOP:45883537)
It is not known whether the participant ever smoked (BDC-HM meaning OMOP:45885135)

Value unknown or not reported: the shared UNKNOWN value of BaseObservationValueEnum, inherited from EducationalAttainmentObservationTypeEnum (no OMOP meaning on HM main). Production uses it for a missing source value; see Observation Metadata. Use UNKNOWN_IF_EVER_SMOKED when the source says smoking history is unknown, UNKNOWN when the answer is simply missing.

Optional; may hold several Context objects, one per circumstance. Records the circumstance the measurement was taken in, relative to an activity: fasting before a blood draw, a bronchodilator before spirometry, exercise, medication use. Fasting and bronchodilator status are ALWAYS recorded here (activity_type FASTING or BRONCHODILATOR_MEDICATION_USE, with relative_timing and, where known, time_duration), even when the concept name already says fasting or post-bronchodilator (for example Glucose in blood - fasting). No context means the status is unknown: never assume pre-bronchodilator or non-fasting.
Not populated for MeasurementObservation. (Free text; production fills category only on SdohObservation.)
Not populated. (A reference to the entity directly measured, for example a specimen; no harmonized concept uses it yet.)
Not mapped from a source variable.

The object that fills value_quantity, range_low, range_high and Activity.time_duration: a number, its unit and, when needed, an operator. On BDC-HM main it is a plain value object with no id of its own. Put the number in exactly one of value_decimal or value_integer.
Use this slot to contain float numbers. This is the usual slot for measured values.
Use this slot to contain integers. Many scores can only be integer values.

Leave empty. Its range is BaseEnum, an empty placeholder enum, so it has no valid value. A range such as 3.4-8.0 does not go here: a reference range goes in range_low and range_high, and a text result goes in value_string.

The unit as a UCUM code (UnitOfMeasurementEnum, from the Units of Measurement ontology), written as the UCUM string, for example mg/dL, mm[Hg], {ratio}, %. Use the concept's target unit from the Concepts file and convert the value when the source unit differs.

Use this slot when the value is reported as being greater than or less than a number. A result below the detection limit (source '<0.15') = value 0.15 with operator LESS_THAN; above the measurable range = GREATER_THAN; a fasting time of '12 hours or more' = 12 h with GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO. Leave empty for an ordinary value.
Example source variable description: Measurable range indicator for C-reactive protein|BNP Character Result

description: The quantity is less than a specified value
The quantity is less than or equal to a specified value
The quantity is equal to a specified value - this will be rarely, if ever used
The quantity is greater than or equal to a specified value
The quantity is greater than a specified value
The object that fills context. It holds activity (required) and relative_timing.
Required. An Activity object (see the Activity rows) that says what was done: its activity_type and, where known, time_duration.

When the MEASUREMENT was taken relative to the activity (the production convention): BEFORE = measured before the activity, as in pre-bronchodilator spirometry; AFTER = measured after it, as in post-bronchodilator spirometry or blood drawn after a fast; CONCURRENT_WITH = measured during it.
Occurring later than: the measurement was taken after the activity (post-bronchodilator spirometry; blood drawn after fasting)
Occurring prior to: the measurement was taken before the activity (pre-bronchodilator spirometry)
Occurring simultaneous to: the measurement was taken during the activity
The object that fills Context.activity.
Use this slot to specify the type of activity. Must be one of the ActivityTypeEnum values below; another kind of activity is a BDC-HM gap.
Abstaining from intake of food or liquid. Use for every fasting-state measurement, including the '- fasting' concepts, with time_duration when the hours are known.
Example source variable description: Fasting time of 12 hours or more [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]

description: The act of taking one or more medication in the class of bronchodilators. Use for every pre- or post-bronchodilator spirometry value, with relative_timing BEFORE or AFTER.
The act of taking one or more medication used in control of diabetes
The act of taking one or more medication in the class of antihyperlipidemics
The act of engaging in aerobic movement
A therapeutic or diagnostic procedure undertaken in the context of healthcare or research, relative to which the measurement was timed

Use this slot to specify the duration of the activity. For example if the fasting was for 8 hours or 12 hours. A Quantity in a UCUM time unit (h, min, d, wk). 'Fasting time of 12 hours or more' = value_decimal 12, unit h, operator GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.
Example source variable description: Fasting time of 12 hours or more [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]|[Fasting information]. Computed fasting time. Q3 [Fasting/Tracking Form, FTRA02. Visit 1]
